pairs.subject: mcp-tools
pairs.evidence: crates/api/src/guards.rs:65 Presenting the one shared admin secret yields an identity-less Principal::Admin that passes every scope check, and 18 of the contract's MCP tools (e.g. enqueue_benchmark) are Access::Admin, so an agent consumer of those tools must hold an omnibus, non-per-consumer credential whose calls cannot be attributed or revoked surgically.

techniques.evidence: crates/api/src/guards.rs:65 Project keys are fine: they are per-consumer, carry a minted key_id and scopes, are read from the store on every call, and name the missing scope. But the admin-only MCP tools need the shared admin secret, which has no identity, and auth_scopes.rs:31 lets it pass every scope. That is the shared-password and omnibus-scope anti-pattern.

crates/api/src/main.rs:87 The agent surface is a stated subset: secret-minting operations are published as off-MCP. Separately, guards.rs keeps the refusals distinct (missing, invalid, key_expired, project_disabled).
crates/api/src/auth.rs:144 Every principal derives a server-verified tenant scope that list operations are evaluated under. This is the 'durable identity exists, so scope it' case.
crates/api/src/auth_scopes.rs:16 Access is declared once in lighttrack-contract, the same table that declares MCP tools, and one router layer enforces it before any extractor runs.

crates/api/src/error.rs:4 This only enables the error-channel split: stable machine codes let the MCP layer route failures without string-matching. The split itself lives in crates/mcp, outside this context.

pairs.registryProposal: When the tool server is a thin pass-through client (here lt-mcp forwards LIGHTTRACK_KEY to an HTTP API), the dispatch door and key registry that authentication-and-scoping governs belong to the backing service, not the tool process. The technique could say explicitly that its per-consumer and no-omnibus rules then bind the backing API's credential model, including any admin secret that tool calls require.
